note: SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION DATA. Every asset, population estimate, shelter capacity, and road segment in this file was invented for the CrisisTwin fire-watch demo. The places are loosely Berkeley-shaped so the coordinates land on plausible terrain, but they describe no real community, no real building, and no real household. No resident data of any kind is used here, and no number in this file counts real people or real capacity.
coordinate_note: Points are given as named latitude/longitude fields. GeoJSON elsewhere in the project orders positions [longitude, latitude]; convert once at that boundary.
representation_note: Every asset is reduced to one representative_point for the point-in-perimeter exposure test. A neighborhood point is a rough centre, not its built footprint; a road point is the midpoint of the endpoints listed with it, not its length.

assets.name: Hills Community Center (synthetic shelter)
assets.note: Capacity is invented. A shelter carries no population_estimate: capacity is not people at risk, and summing it into a population figure would double-count.

assets.name: North Ridge Hall (synthetic shelter)
assets.note: Smallest invented shelter; sits upslope, so it is plausibly exposed in the same run it would be used in.

assets.name: Shasta Road egress (synthetic)
assets.note: Scenario assumption: the only modelled outbound route for the Cragmont Slope cluster. The registry records the dependency; nothing in this package routes traffic over it, so exposure of this segment is not by itself a finding that the cluster is cut off.
